title: Tropospheric Composition and Circulation of Uranus with ALMA and the VLA
question: Determine the physical origin of brightness variations across Uranus's disk and infer the tropospheric composition and circulation pattern between ~1 and ~50 bar.

data.bands: Three ALMA bands at 3.1 mm (98 GHz), 2.1 mm (144 GHz), and 1.3 mm (233 GHz, Band 6)
data.angular_resolution: 0.19 arcsec (2700 km) at 3.1 mm; 0.21 arcsec (3000 km) at 2.1 mm; 0.29 arcsec (4000 km) at 1.3 mm
data.sensitivity: RMS per beam: 0.3 K (3.1 mm), 0.1 K (2.1 mm), 0.1 K (1.3 mm)

what.value: 3.5 cm and older disk-averaged radio brightness temperature data for seasonal comparison

evidence.quote: We explore long-term trends in Uranus’s radio brightness in Figure 4, which plots our VLA 3.0 cm data along with 3.5 cm data obtained by (cite: klein06) and older disk-averaged data from various telescopes (cite: gulkis84)

what.value: Keck near-infrared observations in methane-sensitive PaBeta and H2-sensitive He1A filters from 2015

evidence.quote: Keck observations in the methane-sensitive PaBeta and H$_2$-sensitive He1A filters in 2015 (cite: sromovsky19) revealed a strong polar methane depletion that is spatially correlated with the bright polar region

what.value: Temperature-pressure profile at 1 bar from Voyager 2 radio-occultation and upper atmosphere from Voyager/IRIS

evidence.quote: its temperature follows an adiabat with a temperature of 76.4 K at 1 bar as determined by radio-occultation experiments with Voyager 2 (cite: lindal87).
At higher altitudes, where radiative effects become important, we used the temperature-pressure profile derived from Voyager/IRIS observations by (cite: orton15).
Solar abundances are assumed to be the protosolar values given in (cite: asplund09)

recipe.goal: Calibrate and image ALMA and VLA visibility data (both disk-subtracted and non-disk-subtracted)
recipe.method: Apply standard pipeline/MIRIAD calibration, perform iterative phase-only self-calibration, subtract a uniform limb-darkened disk model in the UV plane for contrast imaging, and invert/deconvolve both disk-subtracted and non-disk-subtracted visibilities, applying a CMB correction.
key_parameters: Self-calibration solution intervals of 20, 10, 5, and 1 minutes
assumptions: Flux calibration errors of ~5% for ALMA, 3% for longest four VLA wavelengths, and 7% at 0.9 cm

recipe.goal: Project maps and extract spatially resolved brightness temperature profiles
recipe.method: Project images cylindrically onto a latitude-longitude grid, extract a 30-degree longitude slice centered on the sub-observer point to create 1-D latitude profiles, and average non-disk-subtracted profiles over 10-degree latitude bins for 25 deg N (20-30 deg N) and 75 deg N (70-80 deg N).
key_parameters: Slice width: 30 deg longitude; latitude bin width: 10 deg (20-30 deg N and 70-80 deg N)

recipe.goal: Fit radiative transfer models to the enriched region (25 deg N) and depleted north polar region (75 deg N) via MCMC
recipe.method: Couple the Radio-BEAR radiative transfer code with the emcee MCMC sampler to fit the 8-band spectrum at 25 deg N using a simplified cloud-physics model, then fit the 75 deg N spectrum using a step-function depletion model above a mixing pressure P_mix.
key_parameters: 500 iterations, 40 walkers, burn-in of 250 iterations (first half discarded)
assumptions: Local thermodynamic equilibrium; dry adiabat with T = 76.4 K at 1 bar (Lindal et al. 1987) and Orton et al. (2015) T-P profile at higher altitudes; cloud opacity ignored; deep H2O fixed at 30x Solar; protosolar abundances from Asplund et al. (2009); simplified model ignores deep water-solution cloud.

recipe.goal: Derive true deep abundances below the water-solution cloud and bulk N/S ratio
recipe.method: Tune the full cloud-physics model (including the deep water-solution cloud) so that the NH3 and H2S abundances between the solution cloud and the NH4SH cloud match the best-constrained retrieved abundances from the MCMC fits, and compute the N/S ratio.
assumptions: Solution cloud removes ~5% of deep H2S and ~25% of deep NH3 following Atreya & Romani (1985); atmosphere is well-mixed below the mixing layer.

evidence.quote: the model is consistent with an NH$_3$ abundance of $4.7_{-1.8}^{+2.1} \times 10^{-7}$ and an H$_2$S abundance of $<$$1.9\times10^{-7}$ between $\sim$20 and $\sim$50 bar.

answer_key.quantity: H2S mixing ratio above P_mix at 75 deg N (1-sigma upper limit)

evidence.quote: the model is consistent with an NH$_3$ abundance of $4.7_{-1.8}^{+2.1} \times 10^{-7}$ and an H$_2$S abundance of $<$$1.9\times10^{-7}$ between $\sim$20 and $\sim$50 bar.

answer_key.quantity: Mixing pressure P_mix at 75 deg N

evidence.quote: The radio spectrum of the downwelling north polar region at latitudes north of $\sim$50$^\circ$N is consistent with strong depletions in both ammonia and hydrogen sulfide from the top of the atmosphere down to a mixing pressure $P_{mix} = 55_{-12}^{+9}$.

answer_key.quantity: Deep H2S mixing ratio (below water solution cloud)

evidence.quote: The radio-dark equator and midlatitudes of the planet (south of $\sim$50$^\circ$ N) are well fit by a deep H$_2$S mixing ratio of $8.7_{-1.5}^{+3.1}\times10^{-4}$ ($37_{-6}^{+13}\times$ Solar)

answer_key.quantity: Deep H2S abundance relative to Solar

evidence.quote: The radio-dark equator and midlatitudes of the planet (south of $\sim$50$^\circ$ N) are well fit by a deep H$_2$S mixing ratio of $8.7_{-1.5}^{+3.1}\times10^{-4}$ ($37_{-6}^{+13}\times$ Solar)

answer_key.quantity: Deep NH3 mixing ratio (below water solution cloud)

evidence.quote: and a deep NH$_3$ mixing ratio of $1.7_{-0.4}^{+0.7}\times10^{-4}$ ($1.4_{-0.3}^{+0.5}\times$ Solar), in good agreement with literature models of Uranus’s disk-averaged spectrum.

answer_key.quantity: Deep NH3 abundance relative to Solar

evidence.quote: This procedure yielded abundances in the deep troposphere of $1.7_{-0.4}^{+0.7} \times 10^{-4}$ (1.4$_{-0.3}^{+0.6}$$\times$ Solar; 1$\sigma$) for NH$_3$ and $8.7_{-1.5}^{+3.1} \times 10^{-4}$ (37$_{-6}^{+13}$$\times$ Solar; 1$\sigma$) for H$_2$S.

answer_key.quantity: Bulk tropospheric N/S ratio

evidence.quote: N/S = $0.20_{-0.07}^{+0.08}$ (1$\sigma$), in agreement with (cite: depater89; depater91), who required N/S$<0.2$.

score_reason: Both ALMA and VLA project codes are explicitly provided, the radiative transfer code (radiobear) is open-source on GitHub, and intermediate brightness temperature tables (Table 2) are fully reported, allowing direct reproduction of the MCMC retrieval even without re-imaging; however, exact imaging parameters, UV disk-subtraction parameters, and MCMC prior bounds are not fully specified.
rediscovery_reason: Public archival ALMA and VLA data with explicit project codes, open-source radiative transfer code (radiobear), and well-defined numeric targets (disk-averaged and latitude-binned brightness temperatures, deep H2S and NH3 abundances, P_mix, and N/S ratio).
